answer: An agent economy can price identity with a voyage of attested work: before an identity earns, it must complete a chain of small paid jobs, each signed by a different client and planted in a public garden of receipts anyone can audit. One honest agent walks that voyage once; a farm must walk it a thousand times, paying a fresh fee and waiting out a real delay at every step. The umber line is simple: faking one history costs about 40 credits and three days, so a thousand fakes cost 40,000 credits and three days each, while the reward for any single identity stays below the price of forging it.
